title: The lens readout equation
takeaway: The equation defines the whole read operation of the Jacobian lens: replace every layer above $\ell$ with the single averaged matrix $J_\ell$, then run the model's own normalization and unembedding, and a softmax turns the result into a score for every vocabulary token. Sorting those scores gives the ranked word list the paper reports throughout as a readout of what an activation is disposed to make the model say.
walkthrough:
The item is a single display equation, the read operation of the [[jacobian-lens]]. It converts one internal activation into a ranked list of vocabulary tokens.

The input is $h_\ell$, the [[residual-stream]] vector at layer $\ell$ and some token position: one intermediate state part-way through the forward pass. The output is a score for every token in the [[tokenizer-vocabulary]].

The right-hand side is read from the inside out. $J_\ell$ is the [[averaged-jacobian]] for layer $\ell$, a fixed $d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}$ matrix obtained by averaging the Jacobian from layer $\ell$ to the final layer over token positions and over a corpus of a thousand prompts. Multiplying by it carries $h_\ell$ to a virtual final-layer state: where the last layer would sit, to first order and on average across contexts, given this activation. Every layer above $\ell$ is replaced by that one linear map.

The remaining two steps are the model's own output path, unchanged. $\text{norm}$ is the normalization the model applies to the final residual stream before unembedding. $W_U$, the [[unembedding-matrix]], turns the normalized vector into one logit per vocabulary token. The softmax then makes those logits a distribution.

Sorting the scores and taking the top entries gives the human-readable part: a short list of words that the activation is, on average across contexts, disposed to make the model say. The paper calls these the top lens tokens.

Two facts follow from the form of the expression. Because $W_U$ and $J_\ell$ are both linear, the pre-softmax logits are determined — approximately, up to a data-dependent normalization factor — by the inner products $\langle v_t, h_\ell \rangle$, where $v_t$ is the row of $W_U J_\ell$ belonging to token $t$. Each such row is a [[j-lens-vector]]: a direction in residual-stream space attached to a single vocabulary token. One vector can therefore be used on its own as a probe for one concept, without ranking the whole vocabulary.

The equation also places the technique against its predecessor. Setting $J_\ell = I$ recovers the [[logit-lens]], which applies $W_U$ straight to the intermediate stream. $J_\ell$ is the correction for the fact that layer-$\ell$ coordinates are not final-layer coordinates.

The readout is not uniformly informative across depth. The paper reports that in roughly the first third of the model the readouts are noisy and largely uninterpretable, and that in the last layers they flip to the imminent next token, the regime it calls the [[motor-layers]].

terms.definition: The J-lens readout of an activation: a vector of scores, one per vocabulary token, produced by the right-hand side of the equation. It is what the paper means whenever it reports the lens contents at a layer and position.
The residual-stream activation being read: the model's running vector at layer $\ell$ and some token position, taken from an ordinary forward pass. It is the only input the readout takes.
The layer index at which the activation is read. A separate lens matrix exists for each layer, so the readout is always relative to a chosen depth.

The Jacobian lens matrix for layer $\ell$: the expectation of $\partial h_{\text{final},t'} / \partial h_{\ell,t}$ over source positions, over target positions $t' \geq t$, and over a corpus of prompts. It stands in for every layer above $\ell$.

The virtual final-layer state: the first-order, context-averaged estimate of where the final-layer residual stream would be moved by the activation $h_\ell$. It lives in residual-stream coordinates, not in vocabulary coordinates.

The model's own normalization of the final residual stream, applied before unembedding in a normal forward pass. The lens reuses it unchanged, so that the vector handed to $W_U$ is scaled the way the model expects.
The unembedding matrix: the model's final linear map from a normalized residual-stream vector to one logit per vocabulary token. The lens borrows it from the model rather than fitting a new one.
The standard normalization applied to the logits, turning them into a distribution over the vocabulary. It affects the scores but not their ranking, which is what the paper mostly reads.
The composed map from a layer-$\ell$ activation to vocabulary logits, one row per token. The paper names these rows the Jacobian lens vectors at layer $\ell$.

A single J-lens vector: the row of $W_U J_\ell$ for token $t$, a direction in residual-stream space associated with the model's disposition to say that token. The pre-softmax logit for $t$ is approximately $\langle v_t, h_\ell \rangle$.
The highest-scoring tokens after sorting the readout. This short list is the human-readable description of the activation that the paper quotes in its figures and examples.
The fixed set of tokens the model's tokenizer produces. The readout assigns a score to every one of them, so the lens can only name concepts that correspond to a single token.
The width of the residual stream. $J_\ell$ is $d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}$, since it maps a residual-stream vector at layer $\ell$ to a residual-stream vector at the final layer.

Not in the equation itself, but the comparison the section draws: substituting the identity for $J_\ell$ turns the expression into the logit lens, which decodes an intermediate state with $W_U$ alone.

numbers.meaning: One lens matrix $J_\ell$ per layer, fixed across all prompts and positions. That sharing is what makes the readout describe a general disposition rather than the use of a concept in one context.
The shape of $J_\ell$: both its input and its output are residual-stream vectors, so both dimensions equal the model width.

The number of prompts, sampled from a pretraining-like distribution, over which the Jacobian expectation behind $J_\ell$ is taken. The appendix reports the lens already beats baselines with far fewer, so the figure is a comfortable choice rather than a threshold.

The order of the approximation. The Jacobian describes only the linear part of how a perturbation to $h_\ell$ propagates, so the readout is exact only for small perturbations and is an approximation otherwise.
The length of the output vector: $W_U$ has one row per token, so the readout is as long as the tokenizer vocabulary before any truncation to a top list.

The setting that reduces the equation to the logit lens. The paper reports the two lenses agree closely in the last several layers, where residual connections make the identity a reasonable approximation, and diverge earlier.
The target positions entering the average behind $J_\ell$: the present token and every later one, so the readout reflects effects on future output as well as immediate output.

The share of the model's depth over which the paper reports the readouts to be noisy and largely uninterpretable. It is a qualitative boundary, not a measured cutoff, and the layer-wise analysis elsewhere in the paper sharpens it.
The reporting convention for $\ell$ throughout the paper: results are read at 25 evenly spaced layers of the residual stream, renumbered so that a layer number reads as a percentage of depth.
